[Rating: 3/10] Did not enjoy this. As with Liger/Riptide, (not in the database) we have a sort of a luckless Backgammon move-back-and-forth-and-bear-off thingy, with no long-term strategy other than to move back and forth and bear off faster than the other guy. They're both [i]way too long[/i] and tedious. I'm down with the idea of repurposing a checkers set, but this is just gratuitous. Would rather play Backgammon, and I hate Backgammon.  At least with the other game, you can stack your checkers on top of the opponent's; even with that incrementally increased interaction, it's still long and boring.

[Rating: 5/10] It starts a bit slow, but the tempo quickly builds as pieces are eliminated and more diagonals open up. Toward the end, it becomes a game of pure tempo, where moves are made to simultaneously block your opponent (without leaving him/her at an impasse) and get into position to either bear off or crown. Interesting, if somewhat light game that can be played with a standard Anglo-American Checker set.
